stem.en: Regeneration of grass leaves after grazing by herbivores is due to:

explanation.en: Intercalary meristems at the base of leaves and internodes of grasses help regenerate grazed parts.

stem.en: Meristems that occur at the tips of roots and shoots are:

explanation.en: Apical meristems are found at the root and shoot tips.

stem.en: The cork cambium is an example of:

explanation.en: Fascicular cambium, interfascicular cambium and cork cambium are lateral meristems.

solution.en: Fascicular cambium, interfascicular cambium and cork cambium are lateral meristems.

stem.en: Lateral meristems are responsible for:

options.en: Increase in length of the root tip

explanation.en: Lateral meristems produce secondary tissues that increase girth.

stem.en: Collenchyma cells are thickened at the corners due to the deposition of:

explanation.en: NCERT: corners are thickened by cellulose, hemicellulose and pectin.

stem.en: Sclereids are commonly found in the pulp of:

explanation.en: Sclereids give the gritty texture in guava, pear and sapota pulp.

stem.en: The simple tissue that performs photosynthesis, storage and secretion is:

explanation.en: Parenchyma is the main living ground tissue performing these functions.

solution.en: Parenchyma is the main living ground tissue performing these functions.

stem.en: Which tissue gives mechanical support to young growing stems and petioles in dicots?

explanation.en: Collenchyma, being living and flexible, supports growing parts.

stem.en: Vessels are absent in:

explanation.en: Vessels are characteristic of angiosperms; gymnosperms lack them.

stem.en: The only living element of xylem is:

explanation.en: Xylem parenchyma cells are living and store food.

stem.en: In roots, protoxylem lies towards the periphery and metaxylem towards the centre. This arrangement is called:

explanation.en: The root condition is exarch; stems are endarch.

stem.en: In gymnosperms, sieve tubes and companion cells are replaced by:

explanation.en: Gymnosperm phloem has sieve cells and albuminous cells.

solution.en: Gymnosperm phloem has sieve cells and albuminous cells.

stem.en: Which statement about a mature sieve tube element is correct?

options.en: It has a large nucleus that controls the companion cell
It lacks a nucleus and its functions are controlled by the companion cell

explanation.en: A mature sieve tube element has peripheral cytoplasm and a vacuole but no nucleus; the companion cell controls it.

stem.en: In grasses, the guard cells of stomata are:

explanation.en: Grass guard cells are dumb-bell shaped; in most other plants they are bean-shaped.

stem.en: The stomatal apparatus consists of:

options.en: The stomatal aperture, guard cells and surrounding subsidiary cells

explanation.en: NCERT defines the stomatal apparatus as aperture + guard cells + subsidiary cells.

stem.en: Vascular bundles in which xylem and phloem lie on different radii alternately are called:

explanation.en: Roots have radial vascular bundles.

stem.en: The cuticle is absent in:

explanation.en: Roots absorb water and lack a cuticle.

solution.en: Roots absorb water and lack a cuticle.

stem.en: A vascular bundle with cambium between xylem and phloem is called:

explanation.en: Cambium allows secondary growth, so the bundle is open; it is typical of dicot stems.

stem.en: Casparian strips, made of suberin, are found in the:

explanation.en: The tangential and radial walls of endodermal cells have suberin deposits called Casparian strips.

stem.en: Lateral roots originate from the:

explanation.en: Initiation of lateral roots and the vascular cambium takes place in the pericycle.

stem.en: A monocot root usually has:

options.en: 2–4 xylem bundles and a small pith
More than six xylem bundles and a large pith

explanation.en: Monocot roots are polyarch with a large, well-developed pith.

stem.en: The parenchymatous cells lying between the xylem and phloem in a root are called:

explanation.en: This parenchyma is the conjunctive tissue.

solution.en: This parenchyma is the conjunctive tissue.

stem.en: The stele of a root includes:

explanation.en: All tissues on the inner side of the endodermis (pericycle, vascular bundles, pith) form the stele.

stem.en: The arrangement of vascular bundles in a ring is characteristic of:

explanation.en: NCERT: a ring arrangement of vascular bundles is characteristic of the dicot stem.

stem.en: In a dicot stem, the endodermis is also called the starch sheath because its cells:

explanation.en: Endodermal cells of the dicot stem are rich in starch grains.

stem.en: Bulliform cells are found in:

options.en: Grass leaves on the upper (adaxial) epidermis
Dicot leaves on the lower epidermis

explanation.en: Bulliform cells occur on the adaxial epidermis along the veins of grass leaves.

stem.en: In an isobilateral leaf:

options.en: Stomata occur only on the lower surface
Mesophyll is differentiated into palisade and spongy layers
Stomata are present on both surfaces and the mesophyll is not differentiated
Vascular bundles are arranged in a ring

explanation.en: Monocot (isobilateral) leaves have stomata on both surfaces and undifferentiated mesophyll.

solution.en: Monocot (isobilateral) leaves have stomata on both surfaces and undifferentiated mesophyll.

stem.en: Which feature is NOT true of the monocot stem?

explanation.en: Monocot stem bundles are closed: they have no cambium.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): The functions of sieve tube elements are controlled by companion cells.
Reason (R): A mature sieve tube element has peripheral cytoplasm and a large vacuole but lacks a nucleus.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Both are true. Because a mature sieve tube element has no nucleus, its functions are controlled by the nucleus of the companion cell; R explains A.

passage.en: Arjun stains a thin transverse section of a young sunflower stem and examines a vascular bundle under the microscope. He notices that the first-formed xylem elements, with narrow lumens, lie towards the centre of the stem, while the later-formed xylem, with wider vessels, lies towards the periphery.

stem.en: What is this arrangement of primary xylem called, and where is it typically found?

explanation.en: Protoxylem towards the centre (pith) and metaxylem towards the periphery is endarch, the condition in stems; in roots the protoxylem lies towards the periphery (exarch).

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Leaves of many grasses roll up during water stress.
Reason (R): Bulliform cells in the adaxial epidermis lose turgor when water is short, so the leaf curls inward and loses less water.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Both are true; when bulliform cells are flaccid the leaf rolls inward to reduce water loss, so R explains A.

passage.en: A student draws the vertical section of a leaf under the microscope. Stomata are present on both surfaces. The mesophyll is not differentiated into palisade and spongy layers. The vascular bundles are all nearly the same size, running parallel to one another, and some large, empty, colourless cells are seen in the upper epidermis.

stem.en: The leaf most likely belongs to:

explanation.en: Undifferentiated mesophyll, stomata on both surfaces, parallel veins of similar size and bulliform cells show an isobilateral monocot leaf such as maize; the others are dicots with dorsiventral leaves.

stem.en:
Read the statements about meristems:
(i) Intercalary meristems occur at the base of leaves and internodes in grasses.
(ii) Lateral meristems are responsible for primary growth.
(iii) The cork cambium is a lateral meristem.
(iv) The shoot apical meristem leaves behind axillary buds.
Which of them are correct?

explanation.en: Statement (ii) is wrong: lateral meristems produce secondary tissues and increase girth (secondary growth). Apical and intercalary meristems give primary growth.

solution.en: Statement (ii) is wrong: lateral meristems produce secondary tissues and increase girth (secondary growth).
Apical and intercalary meristems give primary growth.

stem.en:
Match Column I with Column II:
a. Sieve tube element  b. Companion cell  c. Phloem fibre  d. Xylem parenchyma
(i) Its nucleus controls the sieve tube  (ii) Only dead element of phloem  (iii) Only living element of xylem  (iv) No nucleus at maturity

explanation.en: A mature sieve tube element lacks a nucleus and is controlled by its companion cell. Phloem fibres are the only dead phloem cells, and xylem parenchyma is the only living xylem element.

stem.en: Gymnosperms lack:

explanation.en: Vessels are characteristic of angiosperms, and gymnosperms have albuminous cells and sieve cells instead of companion cells and sieve tubes.

stem.en: In a dicot root, Casparian strips are deposits of suberin on the:

options.en: Tangential and radial walls of endodermal cells

explanation.en: The endodermal cells carry a waxy, water-impermeable band of suberin on their tangential and radial walls: the Casparian strips.

solution.en: The endodermal cells carry a waxy, water-impermeable band of suberin on their tangential and radial walls: the Casparian strips.

stem.en:
Match the organ with its anatomy:
a. Dicot stem  b. Monocot stem  c. Dicot root  d. Monocot root
(i) Scattered, closed bundles  (ii) More than six xylem bundles, large pith  (iii) Ring of conjoint, open bundles  (iv) Two to four xylem patches, small pith

explanation.en: The dicot stem has a ring of open bundles, the monocot stem scattered closed bundles, the dicot root two to four xylem patches with a small pith, and the monocot root is polyarch with a large pith.

stem.en: The meristem that occurs between mature tissues, as in grasses, and helps regenerate parts removed by grazing herbivores is:

explanation.en: The intercalary meristem occurs between mature tissues; it is present in grasses and regenerates parts removed by grazing herbivores. Apical meristems occur at root and shoot tips; lateral meristems (vascular cambium, cork cambium) occur in mature regions and produce secondary tissues.

stem.en: Which simple tissue has cells thickened at the corners due to deposition of cellulose, hemicellulose and pectin?

explanation.en: Collenchyma consists of cells which are much thickened at the corners due to a deposition of cellulose, hemicellulose and pectin. It provides mechanical support to growing parts such as the young stem and petiole of a leaf. Sclerenchyma has lignified walls throughout.

stem.en: Vessels are characteristic of:

explanation.en: The presence of vessels is a characteristic feature of angiosperms. Gymnosperms lack vessels in their xylem (tracheids conduct water). Bryophytes lack vascular tissue entirely.

stem.en: Guard cells in grasses are:

explanation.en: Each stoma is composed of two bean-shaped guard cells in most plants; in grasses the guard cells are dumb-bell shaped.

stem.en: The waxy layer on the outside of the epidermis that prevents water loss is the:

explanation.en: The outside of the epidermis is often covered with a waxy thick layer called the cuticle, which prevents the loss of water. The cuticle is absent in roots. Suberin forms the Casparian strips of the endodermis.

stem.en: In a dorsiventral (dicot) leaf, the elongated cells arranged vertically and parallel to each other just below the upper epidermis form the:

explanation.en: The mesophyll of a dicot leaf has two types of cells. The palisade parenchyma is placed adaxially and made of elongated cells arranged vertically and parallel to each other. The spongy parenchyma below it has oval or round, loosely arranged cells with large air spaces.

stem.en: Fibres of jute, flax and hemp used commercially are:

explanation.en: Phloem fibres (bast fibres) are made of sclerenchymatous cells. They are much elongated, unbranched, with pointed, needle-like apices; the fibres of jute, flax and hemp are used commercially.

stem.en: In roots, the arrangement of primary xylem in which protoxylem lies towards the periphery and metaxylem towards the centre is called:

explanation.en: In roots the protoxylem lies towards the periphery and the metaxylem towards the centre — exarch. In stems the protoxylem lies towards the centre (pith) and metaxylem towards the periphery — endarch.

stem.en: Gymnosperms have ______ in their phloem instead of sieve tubes and companion cells.

explanation.en: Gymnosperms have albuminous cells and sieve cells; they lack sieve tubes and companion cells, which are found in angiosperm phloem.

stem.en: Which of the following are secondary (lateral) meristems?

explanation.en: The meristem that occurs in the mature regions of roots and shoots and appears later than primary meristem is the secondary or lateral meristem — fascicular vascular cambium, interfascicular cambium and cork cambium. Apical and intercalary meristems are primary meristems.

options.en: Root apical meristem and intercalary meristem
Fascicular vascular cambium, interfascicular cambium and cork cambium
Shoot apical meristem and leaf primordia

stem.en: Sclereids are commonly found in:

explanation.en: Sclereids are spherical, oval or cylindrical, highly thickened dead cells with very narrow cavities (lumen). They are commonly found in the fruit walls of nuts; pulp of fruits like guava, pear and sapota; seed coats of legumes and leaves of tea.

options.en: Fruit walls of nuts, pulp of guava, pear and sapota, seed coats of legumes and leaves of tea

stem.en: The functions of a mature sieve tube element are controlled by:

explanation.en: A mature sieve element possesses a peripheral cytoplasm and a large vacuole but lacks a nucleus. The functions of sieve tubes are controlled by the nucleus of companion cells, which are connected to them by pit fields in their common longitudinal walls and help maintain the pressure gradient.

options.en: The nucleus of the companion cell

stem.en: Phloem parenchyma is absent in:

explanation.en: Phloem parenchyma is absent in most of the monocotyledons. In monocot stems, phloem parenchyma is absent and water-containing cavities are present in the vascular bundles.

stem.en: The first formed primary phloem, with narrow sieve tubes, is called:

explanation.en: The first formed primary phloem consists of narrow sieve tubes and is called protophloem; the later formed phloem has bigger sieve tubes and is called metaphloem.

stem.en: In bean-shaped guard cells:

explanation.en: The outer walls of guard cells (away from the stomatal pore) are thin and the inner walls (towards the pore) are highly thickened. The guard cells possess chloroplasts and regulate the opening and closing of stomata.

options.en: The outer walls (away from the pore) are thick and the inner walls (towards the pore) are thin
The outer walls (away from the pore) are thin and the inner walls (towards the pore) are highly thickened

stem.en: In leaves, the ground tissue consists of thin-walled chloroplast-containing cells called:

explanation.en: All tissues except epidermis and vascular bundles constitute the ground tissue. In leaves, the ground tissue consists of thin-walled chloroplast-containing cells and is called mesophyll. Pericycle, pith and medullary rays are ground tissues of stems and roots.

stem.en: Vascular bundles in which cambium is present between phloem and xylem are called:

explanation.en: In dicotyledonous stems, cambium is present between phloem and xylem; such vascular bundles, because they can form secondary xylem and phloem, are called open vascular bundles. Monocot bundles have no cambium and are closed.

stem.en: Radial vascular bundles, with xylem and phloem arranged alternately on different radii, are found in:

explanation.en: When xylem and phloem within a vascular bundle are arranged in an alternate manner on different radii, the arrangement is called radial, as in roots. In conjoint bundles (stems and leaves) xylem and phloem are situated at the same radius, with phloem usually on the outer side of xylem.

stem.en: In a dicot root, lateral roots and the vascular cambium during secondary growth are initiated in the:

explanation.en: Initiation of lateral roots and of the vascular cambium during secondary growth take place in the cells of the pericycle — a few layers of thick-walled parenchymatous cells next to the endodermis.

stem.en: Compared with a dicot root, a monocot root usually has:

explanation.en: A dicot root has fewer (two to four) xylem patches and a small or inconspicuous pith. A monocot root usually has more than six (polyarch) xylem bundles and a large and well-developed pith. Monocot roots do not undergo secondary growth.

options.en: Two to four xylem bundles and a small pith
More than six (polyarch) xylem bundles and a large, well-developed pith
Open vascular bundles in a ring

stem.en: In a dicot stem, the innermost layer of the cortex is rich in starch grains and is called the:

explanation.en: The innermost layer of the cortex is the endodermis. In the dicot stem its cells are rich in starch grains, so the layer is also referred to as the starch sheath. The hypodermis is collenchymatous; the pericycle lies inside the endodermis as semi-lunar sclerenchyma patches.

stem.en: A monocot stem is characterised by:

explanation.en: The monocot stem has a sclerenchymatous hypodermis, a large number of scattered vascular bundles, each surrounded by a sclerenchymatous bundle-sheath, and a large conspicuous parenchymatous ground tissue. The bundles are conjoint and closed; peripheral bundles are generally smaller than central ones.

options.en: Collenchymatous hypodermis and a ring of open bundles
Sclerenchymatous hypodermis and scattered, conjoint, closed vascular bundles each surrounded by a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath

stem.en: In an isobilateral (monocot) leaf:

explanation.en: In an isobilateral leaf the stomata are present on both surfaces of the epidermis and the mesophyll is not differentiated into palisade and spongy parenchyma. Parallel venation is reflected in the near-similar sizes of vascular bundles (except in main veins).

options.en: Stomata are present only on the lower surface
Vascular bundles vary greatly in size due to reticulate venation
The mesophyll is differentiated into palisade and spongy layers
Stomata are present on both surfaces and the mesophyll is not differentiated into palisade and spongy parenchyma

stem.en:
Statement I: The endodermis of a dicot root is a single layer of barrel-shaped cells without intercellular spaces.
Statement II: The tangential as well as radial walls of the endodermal cells have a deposition of water-impermeable, waxy suberin in the form of Casparian strips.

explanation.en: Both statements are correct NCERT lines on the dicot root. The innermost cortical layer, the endodermis, comprises a single layer of barrel-shaped cells without intercellular spaces; its tangential and radial walls bear suberin as Casparian strips.

options.en: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

stem.en:
Assertion (A): In grasses, leaves curl inwards during water stress.
Reason (R): The bulliform cells on the adaxial epidermis become flaccid when they lose water.

explanation.en: Both true and R explains A. In grasses, certain adaxial epidermal cells along the veins are large, empty, colourless bulliform cells. When turgid they keep the leaf surface exposed; when they become flaccid due to water stress they make the leaves curl inwards to minimise water loss.

options.en: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

stem.en: In a dicot root, the stele comprises:

explanation.en: All tissues on the inner side of the endodermis, such as pericycle, vascular bundles and pith, constitute the stele. The endodermis itself is the innermost layer of the cortex and is not part of the stele.

stem.en: Which feature does not belong to a dicot stem?

explanation.en: Water-containing cavities within vascular bundles (along with absence of phloem parenchyma) are found in the monocot stem. The dicot stem has a ring of conjoint, open, endarch bundles, pericycle as semi-lunar sclerenchyma patches above the phloem, medullary rays between bundles and a large pith.

options.en: Vascular bundles arranged in a ring
Conjoint, open bundles with endarch protoxylem
Semi-lunar patches of sclerenchyma as pericycle
Water-containing cavities within the vascular bundles

stem.en:
Statement I: Vessel members are interconnected through perforations in their common walls.
Statement II: Tracheids are living, thin-walled cells with large central vacuoles.

explanation.en: Statement I is correct: a vessel is a long tube of many vessel members with lignified walls and a large central cavity, interconnected through perforations in their common walls. Statement II is incorrect: tracheids are elongated, tube-like cells with thick and lignified walls and tapering ends; they are dead and without protoplasm.

options.en: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

stem.en:
Match the tissue with its feature:
(a) Collenchyma (b) Sclerenchyma (c) Parenchyma (d) Companion cell
(i) Isodiametric, thin-walled, photosynthesis, storage, secretion (ii) Maintains pressure gradient in sieve tubes (iii) Thickened at corners, often with chloroplasts (iv) Dead, lignified walls, mechanical support

explanation.en: Collenchyma — thickened at corners, often contains chloroplasts; sclerenchyma — dead, thick lignified walls, mechanical support; parenchyma — isodiametric thin-walled cells for photosynthesis, storage and secretion; companion cells — help maintain the pressure gradient in sieve tubes.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): In a dorsiventral leaf, the abaxial epidermis generally bears more stomata than the adaxial epidermis.
Reason (R): The palisade parenchyma lies towards the abaxial surface.

explanation.en: A is true: the abaxial (lower) epidermis generally bears more stomata than the adaxial; the adaxial may even lack stomata. R is false: the palisade parenchyma is adaxially placed (towards the upper surface), while the spongy parenchyma lies below it, extending to the lower epidermis.

options.en: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

stem.en: On the basis of structure and location, how many types of tissue systems are recognised in plants, and which one includes trichomes?

explanation.en: There are three tissue systems: epidermal, ground (fundamental) and vascular (conducting). The epidermal tissue system includes epidermal cells, stomata and epidermal appendages — trichomes and hairs. Trichomes on the stem are usually multicellular, may be secretory, and help prevent water loss due to transpiration.
